features.name: op_explicit_comparison_to_established_norms
features.definition: OP's own argument text (title for context): 1 if it explicitly compares the view/subject to an established scientific or historical norm, else 0
features.spec: Read the OP's argument (body), using title only to identify the OP's claim. Output 1 if the OP's own text explicitly compares the subject of their view to an established scientific norm (e.g., accepted scientific consensus, laws/standards of science, established empirical findings) or an established historical norm (e.g., historical precedent, long-standing historical practice or standard), stating a similarity, difference, or conformity/deviation relative to that norm. A mere passing mention of science or history without a comparison, and comparisons to non-scientific/non-historical things (personal anecdotes, current everyday norms) give 0. Exclude quoted text that is from others and not adopted by OP, and edits that merely report replies. Output 0 if the argument is assessable and has no such comparison. Output null if argument is missing or empty/unparseable.

features.name: counterargument_cognitive_complexity
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, all of them, not OP): overall cognitive complexity of the counterarguments on an anchored 0-10 rubric
features.spec: Read title and argument (for context of the OP's view) and every comment in the OC_comments JSON list jointly. Judge only the comments' own reasoning; ignore OP text as a measured source, and ignore quoted text from others except as context. Score the cognitive complexity of the set of counterarguments as a whole (comments pooled, not averaged separately) as an integer 0-10 using this fixed operational rubric: 0 = no reasoning (bare assertion, joke, or insult); 2 = single simple point with little support, one-dimensional; 4 = a claim with some supporting reason or example, little acknowledgement of alternatives; 6 = multiple distinct considerations or perspectives, qualifications, or conditions weighed; 8 = differentiates and integrates several perspectives, acknowledges tradeoffs/nuance, and reasons about their interrelation; 10 = highly sophisticated integration of multiple dimensions, explicit conditional reasoning, and hierarchical synthesis. Length alone does not raise the score. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or the list is empty, or no text is assessable. This is an operational score, not a validated instrument.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.
hypotheses.h0: Mean delta (view change) does not differ between discussions whose OP argument has op_explicit_comparison_to_established_norms=1 and those with 0.
hypotheses.h1: Discussions with op_explicit_comparison_to_established_norms=1 have lower view change than those with 0.
hypotheses.note: Argument may contain later edits; no initial snapshot is assumed. "Established norms" is semantic with no fixed list. OLS on binary outcome (linear probability model).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.
hypotheses.h0: View-change rate does not differ between posts with op_explicit_fear_social_rejection=1 and posts with op_belief_without_emotional_self_defense=1.
hypotheses.h1: Posts with op_explicit_fear_social_rejection=1 have a lower view-change rate than posts with op_belief_without_emotional_self_defense=1.
hypotheses.note: The claim contrasts fear-of-rejection arguments with plain-belief arguments. In the proposed regression the fear coefficient is relative to a omitted residual group (other emotional self-defense without fear, or neither), not relative to the plain group, so no single coefficient equals the claimed contrast (it would need beta_fear - beta_plain). Hence term=null. Subsetting to the two groups is not expressible in the rhs. Fear is probably rare, so power is limited. The hypothesis does not say whether the comparison is adjusted for anything; no controls were added.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cite specific, functioning institutional precedents are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles.
hypotheses.h0: any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent has no association with view change probability relative to any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principle (equal coefficients).
hypotheses.h1: Rows with any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent have higher view-change probability than rows with any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principle (coefficient of precedent greater than that of abstract principle).
hypotheses.note: The claim is a contrast between precedent-citing and abstract-principle comments (beta_A - beta_B), which no single design-matrix coefficient represents, so term is null. Features are row-level any-indicators and can overlap; comment-level comparison is unavailable. Row-level association only; comments are unordered.

hypotheses.note: Linear OLS (linear probability model) assumes a monotonic linear time trend; coefficient is per second (small in magnitude). "Dataset period" taken as the observed timestamp range. Dataset is balanced on outcome, which may affect interpretation of base rates.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that explicitly quote or reference specific textual elements of the original post are associated with a higher probability of the original poster's view changing.

hypotheses.h1: Rows with any_comment_quotes_or_references_op_text = 1 have a higher probability of OP view change than rows with 0.
hypotheses.note: Hypothesis says "discussions containing" such comments; operationalized as any comment. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model. OC_comments are the supplied comments only; conversation (leaky) is not used. argument may include later edits.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the counter-arguments contain direct quotations from the original post are associated with a higher probability of the original poster changing their view.
hypotheses.h0: Discussions with any_comment_quotes_op_post=1 have the same probability of OP delta as those with 0.
hypotheses.h1: Discussions with any_comment_quotes_op_post=1 have a higher probability of OP changing their view than those with 0.
hypotheses.note: Linear probability model via OLS on binary outcome. "Contain" interpreted as any comment (not share/count). Association only; argument may include later edits so quote matching uses current text. No controls added.

hypotheses.hypothesis: ChangeMyView posters receiving substantive counterarguments demonstrate higher levels of view modification than those receiving only supportive comments.
hypotheses.h0: Posts with any_substantive_counterargument=1 have the same view-change rate as posts with only_supportive_comments=1.
hypotheses.h1: Posts with any_substantive_counterargument=1 have a higher view-change rate than posts with only_supportive_comments=1.
hypotheses.note: The claim contrasts two named groups. In the model both coefficients are relative to a residual group (neither substantive counterargument nor only supportive, e.g. neutral or unsupported comments), so no single coefficient equals the contrast; it would need a linear contrast (beta_A - beta_B), which the single-term format cannot represent. Also, all comments are by construction counter-argument comments, so the only_supportive group may be very small. The outcome delta is not used by any feature. Comments have no timestamps and list order has no meaning.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions containing specific counter-arguments citing empirical examples are more likely to be associated with original poster view change than those lacking such evidence.
hypotheses.h0: Discussions with any_comment_cites_empirical_example=1 have the same probability of OP view change as those with 0.
hypotheses.h1: Discussions with any_comment_cites_empirical_example=1 have a higher probability of OP view change than those with 0.
hypotheses.note: Associational only; OLS on binary outcome (linear probability). "Specific" and "empirical example" operationalized by the prompt rubric. Only OC_comments is read, so comments are those supplied, not necessarily the full discussion.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Posts where the original poster explicitly requests emotional support or assistance in the argument text are less likely to result in a view change.
hypotheses.h0: Posts with op_requests_emotional_support_or_assistance=1 have the same probability of a view change (delta) as posts with 0.
hypotheses.h1: Posts with op_requests_emotional_support_or_assistance=1 have a lower probability of a view change than posts with 0.
hypotheses.note: Claim joins 'emotional support or assistance' as one construct; 'assistance' is broad and may be ambiguous. The argument may include later edits, so the request is not guaranteed to be in the initial post. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model. Likely rare predictor.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments introduce concrete, external factual analogies are associated with higher view-change rates than those relying solely on abstract logical refutation.
hypotheses.h0: Discussions with any_comment_concrete_external_analogy=1 do not differ in view-change rate from discussions with all_comments_abstract_logical_refutation_only=1.
hypotheses.h1: Discussions with any_comment_concrete_external_analogy=1 have higher view-change rates than those with all_comments_abstract_logical_refutation_only=1.
hypotheses.note: Claim contrasts analogy discussions with abstract-only discussions. With both indicators, the reference is neither (mostly rows with concrete non-analogy examples), and the claimed contrast is beta_analogy minus beta_abstract, not a single coefficient, so term is null. Restricting to the two groups is not expressible in the rhs. "Abstract-only" is operationalized by a prompt; no frequency cutoff is applied. Comments are only the supplied subset, with no chronology.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument exceeds one hundred words are associated with a lower likelihood of view change than shorter arguments.
hypotheses.h0: argument_over_100_words has no association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
hypotheses.h1: Arguments with argument_over_100_words = 1 have a lower likelihood of view change than arguments of 100 words or fewer.
hypotheses.note: Word count uses whitespace splitting on the current argument text, which may include later edits and quotes; the original-at-post-time text is unavailable. Most arguments exceed 100 words (min 18, 25th percentile 177), so the short group is small. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post's argument explicitly acknowledges potential counterpoints are associated with a higher likelihood of the view changing.
hypotheses.h0: op_acknowledges_counterpoints has no association with the likelihood of delta (view change).
hypotheses.h1: Discussions with op_acknowledges_counterpoints=1 have a higher likelihood of view change than those with 0.
hypotheses.note: Argument may contain later edits, so acknowledgment may not be in the initial post. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model. Observational association only.

hypotheses.note: log_length's construction is undocumented (what text it measures is unknown). The claim is only about the supplied measure, so it is used as-is. The association is observational; OLS on a binary outcome is a linear probability model.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Disclosures of personal emotional vulnerability in the original argument are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.
hypotheses.h0: op_personal_emotional_vulnerability_disclosure has no association with the probability of OP changing their view.
hypotheses.h1: Posts with op_personal_emotional_vulnerability_disclosure=1 have a higher probability of OP view change than those with 0.
hypotheses.note: Binary presence only; no intensity or frequency specified in claim. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model. Argument may include later edits; no initial snapshot is inferable.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A counterargument containing specific empirical evidence is associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster awarding a delta.
hypotheses.h0: any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence has no association with the probability of delta.

hypotheses.h1: Discussions with any_comment_cites_numerical_data=1 have higher likelihood of OP view change than those with 0.
hypotheses.note: Comparison group is "no numerical data", used as proxy for "general assertions"; comments with non-numerical specific evidence are in the 0 group. OLS on binary outcome (linear probability). Associational only.

feature.name: op_explicit_uncertainty
feature.definition: OP's own argument text: 1 if the OP explicitly admits uncertainty or possible error about their own view/claims, else 0.
feature.spec: Read only the argument column (OP post body; may contain later edits, which are not separated out; do not infer an initial version). Return 1 if the OP in their own voice explicitly expresses uncertainty, doubt, or admits they might be wrong about their view or claims (e.g. 'I may be wrong', 'I'm not sure', 'I could be missing something'). Exclude quoted external text, opponents' positions reported by the OP, and generic invitations to respond ('change my view') or hedging of minor details unrelated to doubt about the OP's position. Return 0 if the text is assessable and has no such explicit statement. Return null if argument is missing or empty/unparseable.

feature.name: op_modest_uncertain_epistemic_markers
feature.definition: OP's own argument text (post body, excluding quoted external text and marked edits): 1 if the OP's stance is predominantly expressed with modest/uncertain epistemic markers, else 0
feature.spec: Read only the argument column. Judge the OP's own claims about their view; ignore quoted external text and edit notes (e.g., 'EDIT:'). Return 1 if the OP's central claims are mainly framed with modest, hedged or uncertain epistemic markers (e.g., 'I think', 'maybe', 'might', 'perhaps', 'I'm not sure', 'it seems', 'to my knowledge', 'could be wrong'). Return 0 if the central claims are mainly stated assertively or with high-modality markers (e.g., 'definitely', 'must', 'obviously', 'always', 'undeniably', 'objectively'), or unmarked flat assertions with no hedging. If mixed, choose by how the main thesis is framed. Return null if argument is missing, empty or unparseable. Not an validated scale; no frequency cutoff is imposed beyond the predominant framing of the main thesis.

feature.name: op_argument_has_explicit_uncertainty
feature.definition: OP's own argument text: 1 if it contains at least one explicit uncertainty marker about the OP's own claims/view, else 0
feature.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's post body; may contain later edits, which are not separable, and quoted text). Return 1 if the OP's own voice explicitly expresses uncertainty, hedged confidence or possibility of being wrong about their own view or claims (e.g. 'I'm not sure', 'I might be wrong', 'to my knowledge', 'I could be mistaken', 'I'm unsure', 'maybe I am missing something'). Return 0 if no such explicit marker exists. Exclude uncertainty in quoted external text, uncertainty attributed to others, generic hedges unrelated to the OP's stance (e.g. 'maybe' in hypothetical examples), and moderator/bot notices. Do not count mere invitations to challenge the view unless they state uncertainty. Return null if argument is missing or empty/unparseable.

comparisons.reason: 0 is an any-presence check for an explicit admission of uncertainty/possible error. 1 asks whether the main thesis is predominantly framed with hedged markers. Those are different extraction functions: any versus predominant framing. Marker sets also differ, since 1 counts 'I think' and 'it seems' and 0 requires explicit doubt.

Both are argument-only binary any-presence checks for the OP's explicit uncertainty about their own view, with matching null handling. The pending differences are explicit. 2 also counts 'hedged confidence' and 'to my knowledge' as markers, while 0 does not. 2 excludes moderator/bot notices and generic hypothetical hedges, while 0 excludes minor-detail hedges and generic invitations. Whether hedged confidence counts as explicit uncertainty needs an explicit decision, and the exclusion lists need harmonizing. Both keep their own rubrics as written.

1 measures whether the main thesis is predominantly hedged. 2 measures whether at least one explicit uncertainty marker is present anywhere in the OP's text. Predominance of the thesis framing and any-presence are different extraction functions. 1 also ignores edit notes, while 2 does not separate them.

feature.name: op_asserts_absolute_certainty
feature.definition: OP's own argument text: 1 if the OP explicitly asserts absolute certainty about their view (e.g. cannot be wrong, no possible counterargument), else 0.
feature.spec: Read only the argument column (OP post body; later edits not separable). Return 1 if the OP in their own voice explicitly asserts absolute certainty or incontrovertibility of their view (e.g. 'there is no possible counterargument', 'I am 100% certain', 'undeniably', 'I can't be wrong'). Ordinary confident opinion statements without explicit absolute-certainty claims give 0. Exclude quoted external text and reported opponents' positions. This is not the complement of explicit uncertainty: a post can be 0 on both. Return null if argument is missing or empty/unparseable.

feature.name: op_unwavering_certainty
feature.definition: OP's own argument text (not quoted others, not marked edits): 1 if the view is presented with unwavering certainty and no explicit hedging or self-doubt, else 0
feature.spec: Read only the argument column. Return 1 if the OP presents their view in their own voice with unwavering certainty: assertive/categorical framing (e.g. 'definitely', 'obviously', 'no doubt', flat assertions) AND no explicit hedging or self-doubt markers about their own view. Ignore quoted others and marked edits. Return 0 if any explicit hedging/self-doubt about own view is present, or if the argument is neutral/merely lacks hedging without evident certainty. Return null if argument is missing or unparseable. Do not use title, comments or conversation.

comparisons.reason: Feature 0 requires an explicit assertion of absolute certainty/incontrovertibility (e.g. 'cannot be wrong', 'no possible counterargument'); ordinary confident opinion gives 0. Feature 1 is broader and different: it gives 1 for assertive or categorical framing ('definitely', 'obviously', flat assertions) with no hedging, and 0 if any hedge is present. The two can diverge in both directions: a confident, unhedged post with no absolute-certainty claim is 0 for feature 0 and 1 for feature 1, while an absolute-certainty claim alongside a hedge is 1 for feature 0 and 0 for feature 1. Different constructs and thresholds. Null handling also differs slightly: feature 0 gives null for empty input, feature 1 only for missing or unparseable.

feature.name: distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count
feature.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, not OP) read against the OP title/argument: number of distinct factual premises of the OP's argument that are challenged by at least one comment
feature.spec: Read title, argument and OC_comments jointly. Identify the distinct factual (empirical/descriptive, not value, logical-structure or definitional) premises stated in the OP's title/argument. Count how many distinct such premises are explicitly challenged (disputed as false, unsupported, or inaccurate with factual argument) by at least one comment in OC_comments. Count each premise once even if several comments challenge it; do not count the same premise twice for rewordings. Do not count challenges to values, reasoning, or conclusions only, nor agreement, concessions, or comments challenging things the OP did not claim. Ignore the OP's later edits only if clearly marked as edits; do not use conversation. Output a non-negative integer (0 = comments assessable and none challenge a factual premise). Null if OC_comments is empty/unparseable or argument is missing.

feature.name: distinct_counterargument_count
feature.definition: Other users' comments in OC_comments: number of distinct counter-arguments (semantically distinct challenges to the OP's view) posted across the comments
feature.spec: Read title and argument (for the OP's claim) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP; order carries no meaning). Count the distinct counter-arguments against the OP's view across all comments: each separate line of reasoning/challenge counts once; the same argument repeated in several comments or restated within a comment counts once; comments that are not counter-arguments (agreement, jokes, questions only, moderator/bot notices, pure clarification) count zero. Do not use the conversation column or later replies. Output a non-negative integer. 0 if the list is valid but empty or has no counter-arguments. Null if OC_comments is missing or unparseable.

comparisons.reason: Feature 0 counts distinct OP factual (empirical/descriptive) premises that are challenged by at least one comment, so the unit is the OP's premises. Feature 1 counts distinct counter-argument lines of reasoning across comments, so the unit is the challenges, and these can be value, logical or conclusion challenges. The sources match, but the counting units and eligibility differ. Feature 0 excludes challenges to values, reasoning or conclusions. Feature 1 includes them. Null and empty rules also differ: feature 0 gives null on empty OC_comments or a missing argument, while feature 1 gives 0 on an empty list.

feature.name: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example
feature.definition: Counter-argument comments in OC_comments (not OP): 1 if any comment explicitly cites at least one specific real-world example, else 0
feature.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (each element is one counter-argument comment by a user other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly cites a specific, real-world example (a named or clearly identifiable real event, person, organization, place, study, product, historical case, or concrete real instance) used in the comment's argument. Generic hypotheticals, vague generalities ('some people', 'many countries'), invented scenarios, and mere topic mentions do not count. Endorsement is not needed; the comment itself must present the example. Return 0 if the list is parseable and non-empty and no comment does so. Return 0 for a valid empty list; null if OC_comments is missing or unparseable. Do not use conversation or any outcome.

feature.name: any_comment_concrete_real_world_example
feature.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, any comment): 1 if at least one comment itself provides a concrete real-world example, else 0
feature.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own text, offers a specific concrete real-world example, case, instance, or named/identifiable real situation (e.g. a particular event, person, organization, product, law, study, or personal real-life anecdote) used to support its counter-argument. Return 0 if comments are assessable and none do so (purely abstract reasoning, hypotheticals, generic statements, or only definitions/principles). Do not count examples only appearing inside quoted OP text. Hypothetical invented scenarios do not count. Do not use conversation, delta, or later replies. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty list.

feature.name: any_comment_cites_specific_example
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: explicitly references at least one specific, concrete example or real-world instance (1) vs none (0)
feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of strings, written by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly references a specific, concrete example or real-world instance (a named or clearly identifiable person, event, case, place, organization, product, study, or a concrete particular incident/personal case) used to support or illustrate its point. Purely generic, abstract, hypothetical or category-level statements ('some people', 'e.g. a person who...' without a particular real instance) do not count. Quoted OP text does not count. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none do this. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or an empty list. Do not use any other column.

feature.name: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: cites at least one specific real-world example (1) or none (0)
feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of strings, comments by users other than OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment cites a specific, concrete real-world example (named or clearly identifiable real event, person, organization, study, place, historical case, product, or documented real instance) used in its argument. Generic hypotheticals, vague generalities ('many people'), and purely abstract reasoning or personal hypotheticals do not count; the commenter need not be correct. Quotations of the OP alone do not count. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none cites such an example. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or an empty list. Do not use conversation or any outcome.

feature.name: any_comment_concrete_real_world_example
feature.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, any comment): 1 if at least one comment cites a concrete, specific real-world example, else 0
feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment itself presents a concrete real-world example in support of its point: a specific named or identifiable real event, person, case, institution, study, place, product, or a specific personal/real-life instance. Purely abstract logic, hypotheticals, generic generalizations, or analogies with invented scenarios do not count. Text inside quotations of the OP does not count. Return 0 if the list is parseable and no comment contains such an example (comments rely on abstract reasoning only). Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty, or unparseable. Do not use conversation or any outcome.

feature.name: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: cites at least one specific real-world example (1) or none (0)
feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of strings, written by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment itself cites a specific, concrete real-world example (a named or clearly identifiable real event, person, organization, country, study, case, product, or documented instance) used to support or illustrate its argument. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none do; generic hypotheticals, vague generalities ('many people'), and purely abstract reasoning do not count. Quoted OP text does not count. Examples need not be accurate or persuasive. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or an empty list. Do not use the conversation or any outcome information.

comparisons.reason: Same construct, but empty list: 0 in left vs null in right; left also lacks the quoted-OP-text exclusion and explicit personal-anecdote inclusion.
Same construct; empty OC_comments is 0 in left but null in right; left has no quoted-OP exclusion.
Same construct; empty list 0 vs null; left lacks quoted-OP exclusion.
Same construct; empty list 0 vs null; left lacks quoted-OP exclusion.
Same construct; empty list 0 vs null; left lacks quoted-OP exclusion.

Same core predicate and null rules, but left explicitly counts personal real-life anecdotes (and laws); right says 'documented real instance' and excludes personal hypotheticals without stating whether undocumented personal anecdotes count. Needs explicit decision.
Same any-comment concrete real-world example incl. personal real-life instances, excludes hypotheticals and quoted OP text, null on empty/missing/unparseable.
Same core and null rules, but left explicitly includes personal real-life anecdotes/laws; right limits to 'documented instance' (adds country) with no personal-anecdote rule. Needs explicit decision.
Left explicitly includes concrete personal cases; right requires 'documented real instance' and is silent on undocumented personal anecdotes.

feature.name: any_comment_measured_logical_reasoning
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: contains calm, measured, logically structured reasoning (1) vs none does (0)
feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment presents measured, logical reasoning: a calm, civil tone with explicit premises, evidence or inference steps supporting a conclusion against the OP's view. Merely polite or merely civil comments without reasoning, and reasoning that is accompanied by hostile attacks do not count for that comment. Ignore quoted text from others unless the commenter adopts it. Return 0 if the list is parseable and no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable; an empty list gives null as there is nothing to assess.

feature.name: only_logical_refutation_comments
feature.definition: All OC comments: counter-argue purely by logical/argumentative reasoning, with no comment containing specific empirical evidence; 1 if so
feature.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (order meaningless; ignore conversation). Return 1 if at least one comment refutes the view through logical reasoning (e.g. pointing out contradictions, flawed inference, conceptual distinctions, counterexamples-by-logic) AND no comment contains specific empirical evidence (concrete data, statistics, named studies/sources, specific documented factual cases). Return 0 if the list is parseable and any comment contains such evidence, or no comment offers logical refutation. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty or unparseable.

comparisons.reason: Both read OC_comments and are binary, but the row functions differ. Feature 0 is 1 if any comment has calm, civil, structured reasoning against the OP, and hostile reasoning is excluded. Feature 1 is 1 only if some comment gives logical refutation AND no comment contains specific empirical evidence. That adds a dataset-wide exclusion on evidence. Feature 1 has no civility or tone requirement. Their 0 conditions differ. Feature 0 does not look at evidence, while feature 1 is 0 whenever evidence appears. The two also treat empty lists the same way, but this does not offset the construct difference.

feature.name: quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment (OC_comments): explicitly quotes or directly cites a specific factual claim from the OP's title/argument AND refutes that factual claim.
feature.spec: Read title, argument and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP) jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes (verbatim or a clear close quotation/block quote) a specific factual claim stated in the OP's title or argument and then disputes/refutes that factual claim (e.g. with counter-evidence or reasoning showing it is false or wrong). Merely mentioning the OP's topic, quoting a value judgment/opinion rather than a factual claim, quoting without refuting, or refuting without quoting gives no credit. The OP argument context is required to verify the quoted text and that it is a factual claim. List order is not chronology; ignore the conversation column. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or title and argument are both missing; an empty comment list gives null.

feature.name: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_phrase
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment (OC_comments): explicitly quotes a specific word/phrase/sentence from the OP's title or argument AND argues against/refutes that quoted text.
feature.spec: Read title, argument (OP post) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order carries no chronology/rank) jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes (quotation marks, blockquote '>' or clearly verbatim reproduction) a specific phrase or sentence that actually appears in the OP's title or argument, and that same comment disputes, rebuts or argues against the quoted text. Quote of text not in the OP post (e.g., another commenter), quotes only agreed with, or mere topic mentions/paraphrases without verbatim quoting give no qualification. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none qualifies. Return null if OC_comments or the OP text is missing, empty or unparseable. Do not use conversation or any outcome information; note argument may include later edits and no initial snapshot is inferred.

comparisons.reason: Feature 0 requires the quoted OP text to be a specific factual claim (value judgments/opinions quoted give no credit) and the comment must refute that claim. Feature 1 accepts any quoted word, phrase or sentence from the OP's title or argument that the comment argues against, whether factual or opinion. Feature 0 is a materially narrower subtype. Null handling also differs: an empty comment list gives null in 0, while 1 specifies only missing, empty or unparseable OC_comments or OP text. Retain both as written.

feature.name: purely_logical_refutation_only
feature.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, not OP): 1 if every comment is a corrective/counter-argument and none contains explicit validation of the OP's personal dignity or effort
feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list by other users; order not meaningful) with title and argument as OP context. Return 1 if all comments consist of logical/factual counter-argument or refutation of the OP's view and no comment contains any explicit validation of the OP's personal dignity, worth, or effort (generic politeness or acknowledging a point's logic is not validation). Return 0 if any comment explicitly validates the OP personally or their effort, or if some comment is not a corrective argument at all (e.g. only a question or joke). Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty. Do not use the conversation column.

feature.name: all_comments_pure_refutation
feature.definition: All counter-argument comments in OC_comments: each disputes the OP's view without explicitly acknowledging any valid point of the OP (1) or not (0).
feature.spec: Read title and argument for OP view context and the OC_comments JSON list. Return 1 if every comment challenges or refutes the OP's view and none explicitly acknowledges any valid point, correctness or reasonable part of the OP's view. Return 0 if at least one comment explicitly acknowledges a valid point of the OP (before or after objecting), or if some comment does not dispute the view at all. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty. Do not use conversation or later replies.

comparisons.reason: Both are all-comments binary over the same sources with matching null rules, but the exclusion differs. Feature 0 returns 0 when any comment explicitly validates the OP's personal dignity, worth or effort, and it explicitly says acknowledging a point's logic is NOT validation. Feature 1 returns 0 when any comment explicitly acknowledges a valid point or correct part of the OP's view, which is the very thing feature 0 allows. Feature 0 also requires comments to be logical/factual refutation, while feature 1 only requires them to challenge the view. These are different constructs (personal validation vs. concession of argumentative validity), not a rubric difference to align.

feature.name: any_comment_engages_op_examples_or_premises
feature.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments) vs OP title+argument: 1 if any comment explicitly engages a specific example or premise cited in the OP's argument text, else 0
feature.spec: Read title, argument (OP text; may contain later edits, treat as given) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order carries no meaning) jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly engages with a specific example or premise stated in the OP's argument (e.g. quotes/paraphrases it and responds, rebuts, questions, accepts, or analyzes that particular example/premise). Merely addressing the general topic or the title claim without reference to a specific example/premise from the argument is 0. Endorsement not required. Do not use the conversation column. Return 0 if comments are parseable and none qualify. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or argument is missing/empty. An empty comment list gives 0 if argument is present.

feature.name: any_comment_challenges_op_assumptions
feature.definition: Counter-argument comments in OC_comments (not OP): 1 if any comment explicitly challenges an underlying assumption/premise of the OP's view (as identified from title and argument), 0 otherwise
feature.spec: Read title, argument (OP view; target context) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly challenges an underlying assumption or premise on which the OP's view rests (e.g., says the OP is assuming X, questions the definition, framing or value premise behind the conclusion), rather than only disputing factual claims or the conclusion's facts/evidence. Return 0 if comments are assessable and none do so (including only factual rebuttals, anecdotes, or conclusion-only disagreement). Quoted OP text alone is not a challenge; the commenter must contest the assumption. Do not use conversation or later replies. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty, or title and argument are both missing.

feature.name: any_substantive_counterargument
feature.definition: Non-OP comments in OC_comments: 1 if at least one comment presents a substantive counterargument (reasoned evidence/logic/example challenging the OP's stated view), else 0
feature.spec: Read title and argument (the OP's view) and the OC_comments JSON list jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment offers a substantive counterargument to the OP's view: a reasoned challenge supported by argument, evidence, or example, not mere disagreement, insult, or a bare question. Return 0 if the list is parsed and no comment does so (e.g. all comments are supportive, off-topic, or only unsupported assertions). Ignore quoted text of others unless the commenter adopts it. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or title and argument are both missing; an empty parsed list gives null (no comments to assess). List order carries no meaning.

feature.name: any_comment_well_reasoned_counterargument
feature.definition: Any OC comment (non-OP): 1 if at least one comment directly engages the OP's stated view with a well-reasoned counterargument (explicit reasons/evidence/logic linking to the OP's claim).
feature.spec: Read title and argument (OP's view) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order is not rank/chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment presents a counterargument to the OP's view that is well-reasoned: it addresses the OP's actual claim and supports its opposing position with coherent logic, evidence or specific examples (not mere assertion, insult, joke, question-only, or off-topic). Return 0 if comments are parseable and none qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or title and argument are both missing. Empty list -> null. Do not use any other columns.

comparisons.reason: Engaging a specific example/premise stated in the OP argument (any response type, endorsement not required) differs from challenging an underlying assumption (excludes factual rebuttals). Null rules also differ: empty list gives 0 vs null.

Engagement with a specific OP example/premise is not the same as presenting a substantive reasoned counterargument; a counterargument need not cite a specific OP example, and engagement need not be a counterargument.
Specific-example/premise engagement versus well-reasoned counterargument to the OP's claim; different constructs. Empty-list handling also differs (0 vs null).
Challenge to an underlying assumption (explicitly excluding factual rebuttals) is a materially narrower subtype than any substantive counterargument, which includes factual/evidence-based ones.
Assumption/premise challenge is a narrower subtype than a general well-reasoned counterargument, which can be factual or conclusion-focused.

Both measure any comment with a reasoned counterargument to the OP's view with the same sources and null rules (empty list null). Pending differences: 089 accepts argument, evidence, or example and ignores quoted text unless adopted; 098 requires addressing the OP's actual claim with coherent logic, evidence or specific examples, and explicitly excludes jokes and off-topic. The 'substantive' vs 'well-reasoned' thresholds and the actual-claim requirement need an explicit measurement decision.

feature.name: any_comment_personal_labor_process_detail
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: introduces concrete, personal (first-hand or specific-person) details of how work/labor is actually done (tasks, workflow, conditions, procedures)
feature.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment itself introduces concrete labor-process details drawn from personal experience (the commenter's or a specific named/described person's job), e.g. specific tasks, workflow steps, shifts, tools, conditions, or procedures of actual work. Generic abstract statements about work, hypothetical examples without specific process detail, and quoted OP text do not count. Return 0 if the list is parsed and no comment does so. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty, or unparseable.

feature.name: any_comment_personal_anecdote
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: relates a concrete personal anecdote (commenter's own specific lived experience or event) as part of its argument.
feature.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment's own text recounts a concrete personal anecdote: a specific experience, event or situation that the commenter (or someone they personally know, stated as first-hand) lived through, e.g. 'when I worked at X, ...'. Generic hypotheticals, statistics, general facts, others' reported studies, quotations of the OP, and hypothetical 'imagine' scenarios do not count. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none has such an anecdote. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or an empty list. Do not use any other column.

comparisons.reason: Both are any-comment binary on OC_comments with the same 0/null rules, but the constructs differ. Feature 0 requires concrete labor-process details (tasks, workflow, conditions, procedures of actual work) from a personal or specific person's job. Feature 1 requires any concrete personal anecdote (a specific lived experience or event) on any topic. Feature 1 is broader, since an anecdote need not involve labor process. Feature 0 is a narrower subtype that also admits specific described third persons, whereas feature 1 limits others to people the commenter personally knows, stated first-hand.

feature.name: all_comments_only_abstract_normative
feature.definition: All counter-argument comments in OC_comments: rely solely on abstract normative principles (values, rights, fairness, ethics, should/ought) with no concrete labor-process or personal experiential detail
feature.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than OP). Return 1 if every comment argues solely through abstract normative principles (e.g. rights, fairness, morality, what should be) and none supplies concrete personal or specific factual/process examples. Return 0 if any comment includes concrete examples, personal experience, or empirical/process detail of any kind. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty, or unparseable. By construction this cannot be 1 when any_comment_personal_labor_process_detail is 1.

feature.name: all_comments_solely_abstract_theoretical_rebuttal
feature.definition: All counter-argument comments in OC_comments: rebut using only abstract or theoretical reasoning, with no specific concrete verifiable example of any kind
feature.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by others than the OP). Return 1 if every comment rebuts the OP's view solely through abstract, theoretical, conceptual or principle-based reasoning, and no comment includes a specific concrete example (procedural, factual, case-based or statistical) that could be verified. Return 0 if at least one comment includes any specific concrete verifiable example. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty.

feature.name: any_comment_abstract_reasoning
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: argues through abstract reasoning (general principles, logic, definitions, or impersonal evidence) rather than concrete personal experience.
feature.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (order meaningless). Return 1 if at least one comment's own text makes its case through abstract reasoning: general principles, logical argument, definitions, conceptual distinctions or impersonal general claims, without relying on the commenter's personal anecdote for that argument. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none contains such reasoning (e.g. only anecdotes or non-argument text). Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty. Do not use any other column. A row may be 1 on both this and any_comment_personal_anecdote.

comparisons.reason: Both are all-comments binary on OC_comments with the same null rule and a shared 'abstract only' construct. Pending differences: 0 requires only abstract NORMATIVE principles (values/rights/fairness/should), excluding any personal or factual/process/empirical detail. 1 allows abstract, theoretical or conceptual reasoning generally, and only disqualifies specific concrete VERIFIABLE examples. So the argument type (normative vs. any theoretical) and the disqualifier scope (any empirical/process detail vs. verifiable concrete example, with personal experience not named in 1) differ. Needs an explicit decision.

0 is an all-comments, normative-only, no-concrete-detail measure. 2 is an any-comment measure of abstract reasoning, broader in type (logic, definitions, impersonal evidence) and with different quantifier and empty/zero handling. Any and all are different extraction functions.

1 is all comments solely abstract with no concrete verifiable example. 2 is at least one comment with abstract reasoning, which allows other comments to be concrete and counts impersonal evidence as abstract. The quantifiers differ (all vs any), so these are different constructs.

feature.name: any_comment_asserts_propositional_falsity
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment (OC_comments): asserts that the OP's claim or a premise is factually or logically false (1) vs not (0)
feature.spec: Read title and argument for the OP's view, then every comment in the OC_comments JSON list (ignore order; do not use conversation). Return 1 if at least one comment asserts that the OP's claim or a stated premise is false, incorrect, or logically invalid as a proposition (e.g. disputing facts, definitions or inference), as opposed to presenting harms. A comment may satisfy both this and the harm-quantification feature. Return 0 if comments are parseable and none do so. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty or unparseable.

feature.name: any_oc_comment_introduces_verifiable_external_fact
feature.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments) read against OP title/argument: 1 if any comment explicitly states at least one verifiable external fact not already in the OP's title/argument, else 0.
feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP) jointly with title and argument. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly asserts a concrete, checkable factual claim about the external world (e.g., statistic, historical event, study finding, law, documented example, named source) that is distinct from, and not merely restating, facts or claims already in the OP's title or argument. Opinions, value judgments, hypotheticals, pure logical reasoning, rephrasing of the OP's own facts, and quotes of the OP do not count. Do not use the conversation column. Truth of the fact need not be verified; it must be verifiable in principle. Return 0 if comments parse and none qualify. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty or unparseable, or title/argument is missing. List order is not used.

comparisons.reason: Different constructs. Feature 0 asks whether any comment asserts the OP's claim or a premise is false or logically invalid (a counter-assertion, including purely logical disputes). Feature 1 asks whether any comment introduces a new verifiable external fact absent from the OP, and explicitly excludes pure logical reasoning. A comment can satisfy one and not the other. Null rules also differ: feature 1 returns null if title/argument is missing, while feature 0 does not.

feature.name: any_comment_specific_factual_data_or_citation
feature.definition: Counter-argument comments in OC_comments (not OP, not conversation replies): 1 if any comment provides specific factual data or a verifiable citation, else 0
feature.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment provides specific factual data (e.g., concrete statistics, figures, dates, named studies, named documented events or sources) or a verifiable citation (link, named publication/author/study/law/court case that could be checked). Vague generalities, opinions, hypotheticals, anecdotes without checkable specifics, and bare assertions without specifics do not count. Quoted text from the OP does not count. Return 0 if the list is parsed and no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty. Do not use the conversation column or any outcome.

feature.name: any_comment_cites_numerical_data
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: contains specific numerical data or statistics offered as evidence (1) vs none (0)
feature.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment presents specific numerical data or statistics as part of its argument (e.g., percentages, counts, rates, measured quantities, dated figures, study results with numbers). Quoted figures from others count if the comment uses them as evidence. Do not count vague quantifiers ('most', 'many'), numbers that are merely ordinals/list numbering, hypothetical illustrative arithmetic, or incidental numbers not serving as data (times, addresses). Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none contain such data (general assertions only). Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty. Do not use other columns.

comparisons.reason: Same source (OC_comments), dtype, any-comment structure and null rules, but constructs differ in breadth. Feature 0 counts any specific factual data OR verifiable citation (named studies, sources, laws, court cases, links, documented events, dates) without requiring numbers. Feature 1 requires specific numerical data/statistics used as evidence, so a named case or link with no figures counts for 0 but not 1. Feature 1 is a materially narrower subtype, so they are not interchangeable.

feature.name: op_argument_has_polite_apology
feature.definition: OP's own argument text (post body only): 1 if it contains an explicit polite apology phrase, else 0
feature.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's post body, which may include later edits; do not infer an original snapshot). Return 1 if the OP's own text contains at least one explicit polite apology phrase directed at readers, e.g. 'sorry', 'I apologize', 'apologies for', 'excuse my', 'pardon my', 'my bad'. Count it only when used as an apology/politeness expression by the OP. Exclude quoted text from others, apologies that are only the topic being discussed (e.g. a country apologizing), and non-apology uses of 'sorry' (e.g. 'sorry state of affairs'). Return 0 if the text is assessable and has no such phrase. Return null if argument is missing or empty/unparseable. Do not use other columns.

feature.name: op_argument_tone_policing_request
feature.definition: OP's own argument text (post body): 1 if it explicitly asks/demands that responders adjust their tone, civility, or emotional manner; else 0
feature.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's post body). Return 1 if the OP, in their own words, explicitly requests or demands how commenters should phrase things regarding tone (e.g., 'please be civil', 'don't be rude', 'stay calm', 'no snark', 'keep it polite'), i.e., an explicit tone-policing request directed at responders. Return 0 if no such request. Exclude quoted text from others, subreddit rule boilerplate/moderator notices not adopted by the OP, and mere descriptions of the OP's own tone, and requests about content (e.g., 'cite sources') that do not concern tone. Marked edits within argument count if they are OP-written, though they may be later edits. Empty or unparseable argument: null.

comparisons.reason: Different constructs: OP's own polite apology to readers (e.g., 'sorry', 'my bad') versus OP's explicit request/demand that responders adjust tone or civility. Same source (argument) and binary/null handling, but the predicates differ; an apology is not a tone request.

feature.name: any_comment_specific_verifiable_procedural_example
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: cites at least one specific, verifiable procedural example (a concrete named or checkable process, rule, procedure, case or step-by-step mechanism of how something is actually done)
feature.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment gives a specific, verifiable procedural example: a concrete, checkable description of how a particular process, legal/institutional procedure, protocol, rule or workflow actually operates or operated (e.g. a named statute's steps, a specific court procedure, a documented practice), that could be checked against an external source. Generic hypotheticals, abstract principles, vague appeals to 'how things work', and personal opinions without a checkable procedure do not count. Quoted OP text does not count. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none contain such an example. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty.

feature.name: any_comment_cites_specific_localized_example
feature.definition: Any OC_comments comment: cites at least one specific, localized example (a particular named/identifiable case, instance, event, person, place or concrete situation) as part of its counter-argument.
feature.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment cites a specific, localized example in support of its counter-argument: a particular identifiable case, event, person, place, organization, study instance or concrete situation (e.g. a named country's policy, a specific incident, a personal anecdote with concrete particulars). Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none cites such an example; purely general claims, abstract reasoning, hypotheticals without a particular case, and generic category references do not count. Do not require that the example be correct or persuasive. Quoted text from the OP does not count. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty-unparseable, or not a valid list. Do not use any other column.

feature.name: any_comment_concrete_checkable_example
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: contains at least one concrete, specific, checkable example (named/particular case, event, data point, study, source or link, or observable instance) offered as support, rather than only abstract principles.
feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment itself offers a concrete, specific example that a reader could check (e.g., a named person/event/place/law/study, specific figure, link/citation, or a particular verifiable instance) as support for its point. Return 0 if the comments are assessable and none contains such an example (only abstract principles, generic hypotheticals, or vague unnamed appeals like 'many people'). Examples quoted from the OP do not count unless the commenter adds their own. Do not read conversation or any later replies. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or an empty list. Only the commenter's own text is used; no outcome information.

feature.name: any_comment_specific_example
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: uses at least one specific, concrete illustrative example (1/0)
feature.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment employs a specific, concrete illustrative example to support its point, e.g. a named person, event, case, study, product, or a detailed concrete scenario/instance. Vague generalities, abstract claims, purely hypothetical gestures without concrete detail ('e.g. someone might...'), and examples only quoted from the OP's text do not count. Return 0 if the list is parseable and no comment does. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty, or unparseable. Do not use any other column.

comparisons.reason: 0 requires a checkable procedural/process example (how a procedure operates); 1 accepts any localized example (person, place, event, anecdote). 0 is a materially narrower subtype.
0 is limited to procedural examples; 2 accepts any checkable concrete example (data point, study, link, person, event). Narrower subtype vs broad construct.
0 requires verifiable procedural example; 3 accepts any specific concrete illustrative example, including scenarios and products. Different breadth.

Both are any-comment specific example presence on OC_comments with the same OP-quote exclusion and 1/0/null. Pending: 1 requires a particular localized case/person/place/event/anecdote, while 2 requires checkability and also counts data points, figures, links/citations, studies, laws. Needs an explicit decision on whether checkability and non-localized data/citations count.

Both are any-comment specific example presence with the same source and OP-quote exclusion. Pending: 1 requires a particular identifiable/localized case, including concrete anecdotes. 3 also counts detailed concrete scenarios and products as illustrative examples. Needs an explicit decision on whether detailed non-identified scenarios count and how products and studies are treated.

Both are any-comment concrete specific example presence on OC_comments. Pending: 2 requires the example be checkable by a reader and includes figures, links and citations. 3 requires only a specific illustrative example, with no checkability requirement, and allows detailed concrete scenarios. Needs an explicit decision on the checkability criterion.

feature.name: op_argument_has_counter_question
feature.definition: OP's own argument text (excluding quoted external text and marked edits): 1 if it contains at least one explicit question posed to readers/challengers asking for counter-arguments, rebuttals or counterexamples, else 0
feature.spec: Read only the argument column (OP post body). Return 1 if the OP's own text contains at least one explicit question addressed to readers/respondents that solicits a counter-argument, rebuttal, counterexample or challenge to the OP's view (e.g. 'What am I missing?', 'Can anyone give a counterexample?', 'How would you argue against this?'). Interpretation of 'counter-question markers' is this operational one. Do not count: questions inside quoted external text, rhetorical questions that are not soliciting counters, merely descriptive or topical questions, and text in marked edits/later additions (EDIT/Update sections). A bare question mark alone is not sufficient. Return 0 if the text is assessable and has no such question. Return null if argument is missing or empty/unparseable. Do not use any other columns.

feature.name: op_acknowledges_counterpoints
feature.definition: OP's own argument text (post body): 1 if the OP explicitly acknowledges potential counterpoints, objections or opposing considerations to their view, else 0
feature.spec: Read the argument column (OP post body; may contain later marked edits, which cannot be separated, so read the whole text as given). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly acknowledges that there are potential counterpoints, objections, counterarguments, or opposing views to their position (e.g. 'some may argue', 'I know the counterargument is...', 'I can see the other side', 'one objection might be...'), including anticipating and addressing them. Return 0 if no such explicit acknowledgment exists. Do not count external quotations or other people's positions quoted without OP adopting the acknowledgment of them as counterpoints to the OP's view, mere topic mention, generic invitations to 'change my view', or general uncertainty without referencing counterpoints. Empty or missing argument: null. Output 1, 0 or null.

comparisons.reason: Feature 0 requires an explicit question to readers soliciting counterarguments/counterexamples (solicitation act), excluding marked edits. Feature 1 measures OP acknowledging existence of counterpoints/objections/opposing views (including anticipating and addressing them) and explicitly excludes generic invitations to change view; it reads whole text including edits. Different constructs (soliciting vs acknowledging) and different edit scope.

feature.name: op_has_personal_anecdote
feature.definition: OP's own argument text (post body): 1 if it includes a personal anecdote or first-person experiential narrative about the OP's own experiences, else 0
feature.spec: Read only the argument column (OP post body; may contain later edits, which cannot be separated, so judge the text as given). Return 1 if the OP recounts a personal anecdote or first-person experiential narrative about events or experiences they themselves lived (e.g., 'when I worked at...', 'my friend and I experienced...' as lived by OP). Return 0 if the text contains only abstract claims, hypotheticals, general statistics, or others' experiences with no OP personal experience. Exclude quoted external text, and mere opinion statements like 'I think' without an experience. Null if argument is missing or unparseable; empty text gives null.

feature.name: op_argument_has_personal_anecdote
feature.definition: OP's own argument text: 1 if it contains at least one direct personal anecdote told by the OP (a specific experience that happened to the OP), else 0
feature.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's post body). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, recounts at least one direct personal anecdote: a specific first-person experience or event that happened to the OP (e.g. 'when I worked at X, my boss...', 'I once got denied...'). Experiences of the OP's close family or friends do not count unless the OP also narrates their own involvement. Return 0 if there is none: only abstract reasoning, generic claims, hypotheticals, statistics, third-party or news examples, general statements of opinion or identity without a specific experience, or merely stating a view held ('I believe'). Exclude text inside quotation or block-quote markers that quotes others, and exclude edit notes/responses added after the original text (marked EDIT/Edit/Update). If argument is missing, empty or unparseable return null. Output 1, 0 or null.

feature.name: op_has_personal_experience_narrative
feature.definition: OP's own argument text: 1 if it contains an explicit narrative of the OP's own personal experience (events that happened to or were done by the OP), else 0
feature.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's post body). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly recounts a personal experience narrative: specific first-person events, situations or episodes they lived through or did (e.g. 'when I worked at X, I saw...', 'my sister and I ...'). Return 0 if the argument contains only abstract claims, general reasoning, hypotheticals, third-party or hearsay examples, or opinions without a recounted personal experience; also 0 for passing mentions of identity or a bare stance ('I think', 'I am a student') with no experience recounted. Exclude text inside quotations of other people and moderator/bot notices or edit notes not narrating the OP's experience. Do not use title, comments or conversation. Empty or missing argument: null.

comparisons.reason: Same construct (OP personal anecdote, argument-only, binary, null on missing/empty). Pending differences: 0 judges text as given including later edits, while 1 explicitly excludes EDIT/Update notes; 0 permits friend-shared experiences 'as lived by OP', while 1 requires a specific event happening to OP and excludes family/friends unless OP narrates own involvement; 0 says 'first-person experiential narrative', 1 requires 'specific' experience. Needs explicit decision on edit handling and specificity/third-party involvement.

Same broad construct (OP's own experience narrative, argument-only, binary, null on empty). Pending differences: 0 judges full text including edits (cannot separate), while 2 excludes edit notes not narrating OP's experience (edits that narrate OP experience seem to count) and moderator notices; 2 also explicitly zeroes passing identity mentions and counts events 'done by' OP; wording on 'anecdote' vs 'narrative' and edit scope differ. Needs explicit decision on edit handling and boundary rules.

Same construct and source (argument-only OP experience, binary, null on missing/empty). Pending differences: 1 requires a specific personal anecdote and excludes all edit/Update text outright, whereas 2 excludes only edit notes not narrating OP's experience; 1 explicitly excludes family/friends unless OP narrates own involvement, 2 allows 'my sister and I' style episodes; 2 includes events 'done by' OP and 'situations or episodes' (broader than a specific event). Needs explicit decision on edit scope and specificity.

feature.name: any_comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_diverging
feature.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments) judged against the OP title/argument: 1 if any comment explicitly acknowledges validity of the OP's premise and then introduces disagreement or divergence within that same comment.
feature.spec: Read title, argument and OC_comments jointly. OC_comments is a JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; order is not chronology. Identify the OP's main/initial premise from title and argument (argument may contain later edits; do not infer an initial snapshot, use the premise as stated). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly states that the OP's premise (or a clearly identified core premise of the OP's view) is valid, correct, reasonable or true (e.g. 'you're right that...', 'your historical analysis is not wrong'), and THEN, in the same comment, introduces a point of divergence, disagreement or counter-claim. Acknowledgement must be explicit and about the OP's premise, not mere politeness, thanks, or restating the OP's view, and not acknowledgement of a side point. Quoted text from others and moderator/bot notices do not count. Return 0 if the comments are parsed and no comment does this. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or title/argument are missing; an empty comment list gives 0 only if the list parses as empty.

feature.name: any_comment_acknowledges_valid_point_before_disagreeing
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: explicitly acknowledges a valid point underlying the OP's view, then afterwards introduces a discrepancy/objection (1) or not (0).
feature.spec: Read title and argument (for OP view context) and the OC_comments JSON list (comments by other users; list order is not chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly states that some underlying point, concern or part of the OP's view is valid/correct/reasonable (e.g. 'you're right that...', 'fair point') AND, later within that same comment, introduces a disagreement, counterexample or discrepancy. The acknowledgment must be about the OP's position, not merely about a side fact, politeness, or empathy, and must precede the objection. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none do this (including pure refutations or agreement-only comments). Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty. Do not use conversation or later replies; ignore quoted text from others unless the commenter adopts it.

feature.name: any_comment_concedes_op_component_before_counterexample
feature.definition: Any counter-argument comment (OC_comments): explicitly acknowledges validity of a specific component of the OP's argument and then presents a counter-example; 1 if any comment does so.
feature.spec: Read title, argument (OP context) and the OC_comments JSON list (comments by other users; order is not chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own voice, (a) explicitly acknowledges that a specific identifiable component of the OP's view/argument (a particular claim, premise or point, not generic politeness like 'good post' or a blanket 'you have a point') is valid/correct/reasonable, and (b) subsequently within the same comment presents a counter-example (a specific case, instance or scenario that contradicts or limits the OP's claim). Acknowledgment must come before the counter-example in the comment text. Exclude quoted text from others, reported positions not adopted by the commenter, and bot/moderator notices. Return 0 if the comments are assessable and no comment meets both conditions. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or title/argument is missing; an empty list gives 0. Do not use any outcome or view-change information.

comparisons.reason: Shared construct: any comment acknowledges validity then diverges in the same comment. Pending differences: 0 requires acknowledgment of the OP's main/core premise (not side points); 1 accepts any underlying point, concern or part of the OP's view. Null rules differ: 0 gives null if title/argument are missing and 0 for a parsed empty list; 1 ignores title/argument missingness and gives null for an empty list. Divergence type also differs: 0 allows any disagreement; 1 lists disagreement, counterexample or discrepancy.

0 requires acknowledging the OP's core premise followed by any disagreement. 2 requires acknowledging a specific component followed by a specific counter-example (a materially narrower subtype). Their targets and follow-up requirements differ.

right_feature.spec: Read only the title column (the OP's claim heading; ignore the 'CMV:' prefix). Return 1 if the title's own wording asserts its claim with absolute certainty markers: universal/total quantifiers or frequency terms (always, never, all, every, none, no one, nothing), certainty/necessity terms (definitely, certainly, undeniably, obviously, absolutely, without doubt, impossible, 100%), or equivalent absolute phrasing. Return 0 if no such marker appears, including hedged or merely strong/opinionated wording (e.g., 'almost always', 'should', 'more', 'generally'), or when a marker is only mentioned in a negated/hedging sense (e.g., 'no reason to believe, with certainty' is judged by whether the title asserts absolute certainty itself). Judge the title alone, not body or comments. Empty or missing title: null.

left_feature.name: op_explicit_fear_social_rejection
left_feature.definition: OP's own title and argument text (excluding quoted others, and edits only if not OP's own): 1 if OP explicitly expresses fear of social rejection, ostracism, or isolation, else 0
left_feature.spec: Read title and argument together. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly states fear/worry/anxiety of being rejected, ostracized, judged into exclusion, abandoned, or isolated by others (e.g. 'I'm afraid my friends will stop talking to me if I hold this view'). Fear must be explicit and about social rejection/isolation, not merely disagreement, topic discussion, or fear of non-social harms. Ignore quoted text from others or reported opponents' positions unless OP adopts it. Return 0 if the text is assessable and has no such expression. Return null if title and argument are both missing or empty/unparseable.

Null and empty rules also differ: feature 0 gives null on empty OC_comments or a missing argument, while feature 1 gives 0 on an empty list.

right_feature.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment presents specific numerical data or statistics as part of its argument (e.g., percentages, counts, rates, measured quantities, dated figures, study results with numbers). Do not count vague quantifiers ('most', 'many'), numbers that are merely ordinals/list numbering, hypothetical illustrative arithmetic, or incidental numbers not serving as data (times, addresses). Exclude hedges inside quoted text from others, quoted opponents, and edit notes/moderator notices not stating the OP's stance. Do not count purely generic 'I think/I believe' framing as a hedge unless it expresses uncertainty or limits scope. Return 0 if the argument is readable and contains no such hedging. Return null if argument is missing, empty, or unparseable.
